## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2875a316dc0e8457e53e2c6fced3a1bcf6ee1d5b`

Card #19572 (maintainer 「截流应该要加」), PR #19584, ruling #208 R5 shape: the diff and the card were read, the head's check-runs taken by REST, no derived-gate sweep. Fresh worktree at `origin/main` = `2306a75ecb`, head checked out detached for every local run; self-tests and drives run at 2026-09-21T10:31Z, the positive control at 2026-09-21T10:34Z, the tier reading at 2026-09-21T10:35Z, the check-runs at 2026-09-21T10:38Z. Record written 2026-09-21T10:41Z.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Scope — RIGHT.** `git diff origin/main...2875a316 --name-status` = exactly the eight files (A `scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs`; M the five write tools, `package.json`, `.github/workflows/lint.yml`); +1160 / −0 over three commits (`5fc9ab474d`, `63f55e38c7`, `2875a316dc`); nothing under `packages/**`. The lint.yml hunk is one step, `Write-pace throttle self-test` → `pnpm check:pm-write-pace`, inside the `lint` job (`name: Lint & Repo Gates`, line 179), placed among the other `check:pm-*` self-test steps (post-stamped, label-write, close-cards, the two sweeps), and unconditional — no `if:` between lint.yml lines 1091 and 1823, so it is outside every `select-gate-families` scope and its selftest was not needed. On `check:self-test-wired`: that gate's rule is 「every script CI runs that ships a `--self-test` must have that self-test run by CI too」, collected from workflow `run:` lines and `pnpm check:*` chains; CI runs `write-pace.mjs` only through this very step, so the step is not a mechanical consequence of that gate — it is the card's own item 4 (`--self-test`) made CI-visible in the roster's shape, and it needs no separate R6 sentence: the throttle IS the instrument the maintainer's sentence authorised, and this step is that instrument's self-test, not a second instrument.

**2. The helper's contract — RIGHT at the defaults on every point; one WRONG under a test-only override (D1 below).**
- (a) gap: `decidePace` filters the log to the caller's key, `sleepMs = last + minGapMs − now` (a sibling's future reservation counts as `last`, so a second process paces behind a sleeping first), slept after the lock is released, one `gapText` line to stderr. Driven by the self-test (1 s later sleeps 2 s, not 3; per token). RIGHT.
- (b) budget: trailing 60 min, `inWindow.length ≥ hourlyMax` → `exhausted`, `exit(10)`, no sleep, prescription naming the count, the reopen instant (`min(inWindow) + 60 min`) and the fold advice; a refused write reserves nothing. Driven at budget 1: the 2nd write → `exhausted`, exits `[10]`, slept `[]`, text names 「1 write(s) … budget (1) … number 2 … reopens at (one hour after the injected clock)」. RIGHT at the defaults. ⛔ WRONG at `OS_PM_WRITE_HOURLY_MAX=0` — see D1.
- (c) stop marker: `stopSignalFrom` fires on 429; on 403 whose body matches `secondary rate limit` or `abuse detection`; on any `retry-after` (seconds or HTTP-date); on `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0` at ANY status; and on `verdict === 'ratelimit'` handed in by value. Duration `max(30 min, retry-after)`. Driven: 200 + remaining 0 → 30 min marker; 503 + retry-after HTTP-date 3 h → 180 min; a secondary-limit 403 with remaining 4999 and verdict `refusal` → marker recorded, the next write → `stopped`, exit 10, the expiry printed (`stoppedText` carries `until STAMP`). RIGHT.
- (d) key: `sha256(token.trim()).hex.slice(0, 12)`; an empty token keys to `no-token` (still paced). My own drive with a fixture token: the log holds `{"t":…,"k":"87f62e9ce4ad",…}` and the marker line; `grep -rl` of the token value over every file the drive wrote hits only the drive script itself, never the log. `--status` prints the key, never the token. RIGHT.
- (e) env: the only reads are `OS_PM_WRITE_PACE_FILE` (`paceFilePath`), `OS_PM_WRITE_MIN_GAP_MS` and `OS_PM_WRITE_HOURLY_MAX` (`limitsFrom`); `--status` reads `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` for the identity, which is the token, not an override. A malformed override falls back to the default and says so. RIGHT.
- (f) the three fail-closed fixes in `2875a316dc`: (i) an unwritable log — `withPaceLock` swallows its own parent-mkdir failure, the poll breaks at once on a non-`EEXIST` error, `fn()` throws from `writeRecordsTo`, `paceWrite` catches → `unrecordableText` naming the path and the `OS_PM_WRITE_PACE_FILE` remedy, `exit(10)`; driven under a REAL poll sleep: returns `unrecordable`, exits `[10]`, 0 ms. (ii) `noteResponse` wraps the whole lock in try/catch, logs the consequence (「the NEXT write … will NOT be refused」) and returns `recorded: false`; the self-test drives it on the same unwritable path. (iii) the lock loop is `attempt below 400 AND now() below deadline`; a held lock under a frozen clock with a real 40 ms poll returns after at most 400 × 40 ms = 16 s and fails open; an unusable path breaks the loop on the first non-`EEXIST`. Neither a frozen clock nor an unusable path can hang. RIGHT.

**3. Wiring — RIGHT; one WRONG in the prescription's prose (D2 below).** Each of the five tools has exactly ONE `fetch(` (post-stamped 2548, label-write 338, close-cards 448, sweep-closed-cards 503, sweep-stale-finding 361); each computes `paced = isWriteMethod(method)`, awaits `paceWrite` before the fetch and calls `noteResponse` after it (both the refusal path and the 2xx path in the three that throw on `!res.ok`; the one shared exit in label-write and close-cards, which never throw on status), so GET is never paced. The write-verb census over `scripts/pm/*.mjs` is twelve sites in exactly those five files; no other `.mjs` under `scripts/pm` issues a write verb and none spawns `gh`/`curl`; the self-test's last battery pins that roster against `git ls-files`. Dry runs: `post-stamped` returns from `if (options.dryRun)` before `writeArtefact` (its only in-dry-run REST call is a GET probe); label-write's dry run returns before its plan runs; the sweeps act only under `--write`. Positive control, measured: `OS_PM_WRITE_HOURLY_MAX=0 OS_PM_WRITE_MIN_GAP_MS=600000 node scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs --dry-run --comment=1 --file=BODY --repo=objectstack-ai/objectstack` → exit 0, stdout and stderr byte-identical to the un-overridden run after stamp normalisation, and no pace file created. Label-write: each call in its step-③ plan (label POST, label DELETE per removal, assignee POST, assignee DELETE), the whole-set PATCH fallback and the step-④ re-add POST each go through `rest()`, so each is counted and gapped. The director's question: between the label POST and the read-back GET there is no paced call, so the refusal cannot land in exactly that gap — the read-back is a GET and always runs after a POST that returned. It CAN land between two step-③ calls (label POST landed, then the label DELETE refused — a two-state card), before the fallback PATCH (nothing landed there: the additive verb was refused), and before the re-add POST after a strip. What the tool prints then: its `③ 写 — POST … HTTP 200 (ok)` line for the call that landed, then the throttle's refusal block, and the process exits 10 from inside `rest()` — the read-back does NOT run, no `④` line prints, and label-write's own 「The board may be PARTIALLY written — the calls above say which landed」 never prints. Close-cards: the comment goes through a post-stamped CHILD, whose exit 10 close-cards already reports honestly (「comment REFUSED — post-stamped exit 10 … NOTHING was written … Stopping」); its closing PATCH is in-process, so a refusal there leaves the comment landed and the card open, with `halfWriteText` bypassed by the exit.

**4. `classifyHttp` reuse — RIGHT.** `write-pace.mjs` imports nothing from `label-write.mjs`; `stopSignalFrom` takes `verdict` by value and its own arms are the four signals `classifyHttp` does not answer (a 429 with quota left, a 403 whose BODY names the secondary limit, a bare `retry-after`, remaining 0 on any status). The overlap on a 429/403 with remaining 0 yields the same marker either way, not a second classification. The dev's finding is confirmed by reading `classifyHttp` (line 311: `ratelimit` only when `rateRemaining === 0`, else line 313 `refusal`) and by the drive in 2(c): `noteResponse` runs inside `rest()` before the verdict is returned to `runLabelWrite`, so the marker is on disk before the fallback `doCall('card-patch', …)` calls `paceWrite`, which refuses it at exit 10. Reliable as long as the log is writable — the only gap is a log that became unwritable between the POST and the PATCH, in which case the earlier `paceWrite` would already have refused. Post-stamped hands `platformRefusalText(text)` as the body, which keeps the JSON `message` (where the platform puts the sentence); the sweeps hand the raw text; label-write and close-cards hand the parsed object, which `namesSecondaryLimit` stringifies — and a `retry-after` on the same answer marks it regardless.

**5. Self-tests — RIGHT.** On head `2875a316dc`: `write-pace --self-test` exit 0, 「69 cases pass across 9 batteries」; `post-stamped` exit 0 (544 cases / 18 batteries); `label-write` exit 0 (75 / 9); `close-cards` exit 0 (102 / 11); `sweep-closed-cards` exit 0 (87 / 9); `sweep-stale-finding` exit 0 (91 / 9). The case names cover the 41st write (「the 41st is refused」, 「…with the distinct exit code」, 「…and it did NOT sleep instead」, 「a refused write reserves NOTHING」), the unwritable log (「a log it cannot write REFUSES the write」), the frozen-clock lock (「a held lock under a FROZEN clock still returns」), the marker from a 429, the prune battery (expired marker dropped, two-hour marker kept, torn line dropped, file rewritten pruned), and 「THE case: the token never appears in the file, in any field」. Floor is a battery-name roster (9 batteries, per-battery minimums) with the `selfTestReachedVerdict` handshake at the dispatch. `--status` prints seven labelled lines to stdout (`file`, `token key`, `budget N of 40 · M left`, `gap`, `marker`, `verdict`, the READ notice), exit 0, and creates no file.

**Defects found (neither reaches the contract at its defaults):**
- **D1 — WRONG, test-only path.** `OS_PM_WRITE_HOURLY_MAX=0` on a LIVE write: `decidePace` returns `exhausted` with `resumeAtMs = Math.min() + WINDOW_MS = Infinity`, and `exhaustedText` → `stampUtc(Infinity)` throws `RangeError: Invalid time value` out of `paceWrite`, out of the transport, before any refusal line and before `exit(10)`. Driven: 「THREW RangeError Invalid time value, exits before throw [], 0 lines logged」. Reachable only when `hourlyMax` is 0 (the sole way `inWindow` is empty at `exhausted`), so the defaults are untouched; but the PR body describes exactly these settings as 「would refuse ANY paced write at exit 10」, which is not what they do. The positive control's evidence survives (exit 0, identical output, no file — a crash would have been louder still). One-line fix in `decidePace` (`inWindow.length ? Math.min(...inWindow) + WINDOW_MS : nowMs`) plus a case beside 「zero is a real value」.
- **D2 — WRONG in the prescription's prose; a reporting gap on mid-run refusals.** `exhaustedText` says 「nothing was written, nothing is half-written, and this process will not retry」 and the header adds 「re-running after the printed instant is safe」. Because the refusal is a `process.exit(10)` from INSIDE the transport, in a run that already landed a write (label-write's plan and re-add, close-cards' PATCH after its comment, sweep-closed-cards' POST after its DELETEs) those sentences are false for that run, and the tools' own half-state reporters never print (item 3). Close-cards re-run after a mid-card refusal re-posts the closing comment. Follow-up: narrow the sentence to this write, and let the tools route on a typed refusal so their reporters print before the exit — its own card, not a rider.

**Nits, not blocking:** (N1) the frozen-clock lock case compares the injected `T0` (a fixed 2026-09-21 10:00 UTC constant in the source) with the fixture lock's REAL mtime, so it takes the attempt-bound path only because the wall clock is now after `T0`; a clock before 09:59:45Z that day steals the lock and fails 「never stolen」 (my drive at an injected 12:00Z stole it in 40 ms) — pin the fixture's mtime with `utimesSync`. (N2) the PR body is stale against the head: 64 cases, +1082 and head `63f55e38c7` in its Landing-tier block vs 69, +1160 and `2875a316dc`; the card's os-dev-report carries the current numbers. (N3) when the lock fails open, the whole-file rewrite can drop a freshly written STOP MARKER as well as undercount a write; the header names only the undercount.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no — carriers: none hung. Nothing under `packages/**`; `skip-changeset` is on the PR; no changeset, correctly.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on `2875a316dc` at the reading: `Lint & Repo Gates` success (id 106293792677), `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Test Core` success, `Dogfood Regression Gate` success, `Build Core` success, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success — 7 of 7 required contexts `completed` / `success`; none in progress at that reading.
- Labels on the PR: `ci/cd`, `size/xl`, `dependencies`, `skip-changeset`. Draft, no auto-merge, no comments before this one.
- Tier: `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --branch claude/issue-19572-write-pace` → exit 0, 「governed-surface predicate: 0 of 8 path(s) hit the register (6 surfaces)」, 「NOT governed — ordinary queue landing applies」, size 1160 ≤ 5000. The card's 「Tier S」 line and the register disagree; the register is the authority (Prime Directive #14) and that question is not this PR's — the director lands it through the ordinary queue on green after this record.
- Writes by this review: this one comment, through the `origin/main` copy of `post-stamped.mjs` from a worktree at `2306a75ecb`. No MCP GitHub tool, no label, no ready flip, no auto-merge, no body edit, no issue.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19572-write-pace`
Reviewed-by: `session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`

**VERDICT: PASS** — the contract holds at its defaults on every item, driven and read; D1 and D2 are named follow-ups for the director's landing decision (D1 is a one-line fix whose new head would need a fresh record; D2 is its own card).
